findings.reason: a worker cannot make this control deterministic without a decision the plan does not settle (defer warmup until after `initialize`, or exempt the deliberate background imports from the prohibited set), and an indeterminate head arm will be read as a failing gate and invites weakening the control rather than repairing it.
findings.text: the guard requires a test to fail when the discovery commands or the schema runtime are imported before the server answers `initialize`, but importing `imas_codex.llm.server` — which `serve` does immediately — calls `warmup.start()` at module load (`imas_codex/llm/server.py:83`), and its `discovery` and `graph` groups import `imas_codex.discovery` and `imas_codex.graph`/`graph.schema` in background threads (`imas_codex/llm/_warmup.py:98-124`), so at head the guard fails whenever those threads win the race with the handshake and passes when they lose; the documented head design keeps that warmup rather than removing it

findings.reason: with no stated base quantity for the arm and no consistent breakdown to attribute against, the node will either fail an unreachable 90 % target or substitute its own denominator, and the receipt will not show what the gate claims to show.
findings.text: the 90 % attribution arm is measured against "the base revision's wall time to first answer", which §1 gives as 35.1 s, while every number the plan offers comes from the `--help` profile (19.9 s of 27.5 s), so the arm silently demands about 31.6 s of attributed time — some 11.7 s beyond anything the plan has measured — and §1's own breakdown does not add up: 11.5 s of language-model client plus 4.6 s of schema runtime plus 3.9 s of facility configuration is 20.0 s against the 18.6 s they are said to arrive through, so a reader cannot tell whether the parts are additive, nested, or double-counted

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the spawn anchor `.mcp.json` at the repository root exists and invokes `uv run --no-sync --project ${HOME}/Code/imas-codex imas-codex serve`, which is the form §2 says the server is spawned as; the cited evidence directory resolves; no extensionless href is cited.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — the new import guard at §2 line 52 forbids importing the discovery commands and the schema runtime before `initialize` is answered, while the server's own import path starts background warmup threads that import exactly those packages at module load, so the head arm of that control is a race rather than a measure.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §2 line 45 names `docs/evidence/fragments/serve-answers-inside-the-connect-limit/`, which exists in the tree and is tracked (`briefs/lazy-command-group.md`), so the timings, loads and base arms land on a durable committed path rather than a scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the section and its done-when name outcomes (cold starts, first answer, named parts) rather than symbols, and carry no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or changelog prose.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the attribution arm at §2 line 50 is scored against a base quantity §1 never measured and rests on a breakdown whose parts exceed the total they are said to sum to, and the section prescribes no implementation, which is correct.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §2 has one deliverable (the server's time to first answer), and each done-when arm measures a facet of it: the quiet-node median, the loaded-node starts, the attribution receipt, the command-line cost, the import guard, tool-name parity and command-list parity.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — the plan declares itself standalone with no depends-on, informs or gates to name, and its one section-to-followup link (f-saicl-001, whose prompt names §2) resolves to a section that exists.
